entries.name: Actual Budget
entries.summary: Budget by envelopes, with your accounts kept on your own server.
entries.description:
Actual Budget is a personal finance app built around envelope budgeting: the
money you earn is each given a job. It syncs between your devices through
this server and can import from YNAB, QIF, OFX and CSV files. The first visit
sets the server's password.

entries.name: AdGuard Home
entries.summary: Block ads and trackers for every device on your network.
entries.description:
A network-wide ad and tracker blocker that works as your home DNS server.
Because other devices depend on it, this Node keeps a fixed address and
starts AdGuard Home before anything else.

entries.name: Audiobookshelf
entries.summary: Your audiobooks and podcasts, streamed to every device, each listener's place kept.
entries.description:
Audiobookshelf serves your audiobooks and podcasts to its phone apps and any browser.
It fetches covers and chapters, downloads new podcast episodes, and keeps each
listener's progress in step across devices. The first visit creates its admin account.

entries.name: Bazarr
entries.summary: Find and download subtitles for the films and series Sonarr and Radarr keep.
entries.description:
Bazarr looks up subtitles in the languages you want for everything in your Sonarr and Radarr libraries, and keeps them up to date.
The first visit sets up its login.

entries.name: Calibre-Web
entries.summary: Browse, read and download the ebooks of your Calibre library.
entries.description:
Calibre-Web gives your Calibre library a web page: browse and search your books,
read them in the browser, send them to an ereader or download them. Point it at
the shared folder that holds your library's metadata.db. Sign in first as admin
with the password admin123, then change it.

settings.label: Run Calibre-web as this group id.
Run Calibre-web as this user id.

entries.name: Changedetection.io
entries.summary: Watch web pages and get told when they change: prices, stock, news.
entries.description:
Changedetection.io checks the pages you give it on a schedule and tells you
what changed, by email, ntfy, Gotify and many more. It has no password until
you set one in its settings.

entries.name: code-server
entries.summary: VS Code in the browser, running on your server.
entries.description:
code-server runs VS Code on the Node, so you can edit code and use a terminal
from any browser. Its password is made up at install; copy it from the
Service's settings.

settings.label: Password for sudo in its terminal

entries.name: ESPHome
entries.summary: Write and flash firmware for ESP32 and ESP8266 boards, and see them online.
entries.description:
ESPHome turns cheap ESP32 and ESP8266 boards into sensors and switches for
Home Assistant: describe a device in YAML, build its firmware and update it
over the air. Flash a new board from the browser over USB.

grants.why: Finds your ESPHome devices on the home network by their mDNS announcements, to show which are online and update them by name. Its page is then also open on your home network at the Node's address, port 6052.
grants.without: Devices are checked by ping instead, and updated by address.

entries.name: Forgejo
entries.summary: Host your own Git repositories, with issues, pull requests and CI.
entries.description:
Forgejo is a community-run Git forge. Keep your code and its history on your
own Nodes, review changes in pull requests, track issues, and push over
HTTPS or SSH (port 2222 on the Node).

entries.name: FreshRSS
entries.summary: Follow websites, blogs and news through their feeds, in one place.
entries.description:
FreshRSS gathers the RSS and Atom feeds you follow and lets you read them in one
list, in the browser or in any app that speaks its API. The first visit runs its
setup, where you create your account.

entries.name: Gotify
entries.summary: Send push notifications to your phone from your own server.
entries.description:
Gotify receives messages from scripts and apps over a simple REST API and
pushes them to its Android app and the browser. Sign in as admin with the
password made up at install.

entries.name: Homarr
entries.summary: A start page for your home server, with every app and its status in one place.
entries.description:
Homarr is a dashboard: arrange tiles for your apps, bookmarks and widgets
(weather, calendars, media, downloads) and see at a glance what is up. The
first visit creates its admin account.

settings.label: Key that encrypts its stored secrets

entries.name: Home Assistant
entries.summary: Control your lights, heating, plugs and sensors from one place, without the cloud.
entries.description:
Home Assistant connects the smart devices in your home, from lights and
thermostats to plugs, sensors and speakers, and lets you control them
together and automate them, all from your own server. The first visit
creates its owner account.

Its add-on store is part of Home Assistant OS and not of this install; the
usual add-ons, such as Mosquitto and Zigbee2MQTT, are Services of their own.
Bluetooth and Zigbee or Z-Wave sticks plugged into the Node are not yet
available to it here.

grants.why: Finds the devices on your home network by listening for their announcements (Chromecast, Sonos, HomeKit, smart plugs and most local integrations), and answers HomeKit on its own ports. Its page is then also open on your home network at the Node's address, port 8123.
grants.without: Add devices by their address. Integrations that find devices by themselves, and HomeKit, will not work.

entries.name: Immich
entries.summary: Back up and browse your photos and videos, with search by faces and things.
entries.description:
Immich keeps your photos and videos on your own Nodes. The phone apps back
them up as you take them; the web page browses them by date, place, people
and what is in them, found by its own machine learning.

database

entries.name: IT Tools
entries.summary: Handy tools for developers: encoders, converters, generators and more.
entries.description:
IT Tools is a collection of small tools in the browser: base64 and URL
encoders, hash and UUID generators, JSON and YAML converters, colour pickers and
many more. It keeps nothing and has no accounts.

entries.name: Jellyfin
entries.summary: Stream your movies, shows and music to any device.
entries.description:
Jellyfin is a free media system. Point it at your films, series, music and
photos and watch them from your TV, phone or browser.

entries.name: Jellyseerr
entries.summary: Let your household ask for films and series, and send them to Sonarr and Radarr.
entries.description:
Jellyseerr shows what is on your Jellyfin, Emby or Plex server and lets the
people who use it ask for more; approved requests go to Sonarr and Radarr. The
first visit connects it to your media server.

entries.name: Kavita
entries.summary: Read your comics, manga and ebooks in the browser, with your place kept.
entries.description:
Kavita serves your comics, manga and ebooks from a shared folder, with a
reader in the browser and OPDS for reading apps. The first visit creates its
admin account.

entries.name: Lidarr
entries.summary: Follow your favourite artists and fetch their new albums.
entries.description:
Lidarr watches for new releases from the artists you follow, sends them to your download client and files them in your music folder, named and tagged.
The first visit sets up its login.

entries.name: linkding
entries.summary: Save, tag and search your bookmarks, with copies of the pages kept.
entries.description:
linkding is a bookmark manager: save links from its browser extension or
bookmarklet, tag them, search them, and keep a copy of each page in case it
disappears. Sign in as admin with the password made up at install.

entries.name: Mealie
entries.summary: Keep your recipes, plan the week's meals and make the shopping list.
entries.description:
Mealie keeps your family's recipes. Paste a recipe's web address and it
imports the ingredients and steps, or type one in. Plan meals for the week and
turn them into a shopping list. Sign in first as changeme@example.com with the
password MyPassword, then change both.

entries.name: Memos
entries.summary: Quick notes in Markdown, tagged and kept on your own server.
entries.description:
Memos is a place for short notes: thoughts, links, lists and drafts, written in
Markdown and found again by tag or search. The first account created is its admin.

entries.name: Minecraft Server
entries.summary: A Minecraft Java Edition server for you and your friends.
entries.description:
Runs a Minecraft Java Edition server (vanilla by default) that players
on your network can join at this Node's address. Turn on "Reachable from
the internet" in the Console to let friends elsewhere join too; the Node
asks your router to forward the game port for you.

settings.label: I accept the Minecraft End User License Agreement (minecraft.net/eula)
Message shown in the server list

entries.name: Mosquitto
entries.summary: An MQTT broker, the message hub Home Assistant, Zigbee2MQTT and smart devices talk through.
entries.description:
Mosquitto passes MQTT messages between the devices and apps of your home:
sensors publish, Home Assistant and Node-RED subscribe. Devices on your home
network reach it at the Node's address, port 1883. It runs without passwords,
so anything on your home network can publish and subscribe.

entries.name: n8n
entries.summary: Automate work across your apps and services, with workflows built in the browser.
entries.description:
n8n connects apps and services in workflows: when something happens in one,
do something in others, with hundreds of integrations and code where you need
it. The first visit creates its owner account.

entries.name: Navidrome
entries.summary: Music Collection and Streaming Server
entries.description: Navidrome is an open source web-based music collection server and streamer. It gives you freedom to listen to your music collection from any browser or mobile device. It's like your personal Spotify!

entries.name: Nextcloud
entries.summary: Content collaboration platform
entries.description:
Discover the ultimate solution for remote collaboration with Nextcloud. Unlike traditional office software, Nextcloud seamlessly integrates files, communication, and productivity tools into one platform, enhancing teamwork and streamlining your workflow. Say goodbye to the limitations of conventional tools and embrace a new era of collaboration.

Nextcloud stands out with its robust features tailored for every need. Enjoy secure file storage, real-time communication via Talk, comprehensive groupware, and powerful office integration, all in one place. Experience these top-notch features at an affordable price, making it accessible for everyone to elevate their collaboration game.

Deploying Nextcloud on a Zima private cloud device brings unparalleled convenience. Benefit from unlimited storage, secure data privacy, local network speeds, and multi-device access, ensuring you have everything you need at your fingertips.

entries.name: Node-RED
entries.summary: Wire devices, services and APIs together into automations, in the browser.
entries.description:
Node-RED builds automations by connecting nodes in a flow: MQTT messages,
Home Assistant events, web requests, timers and hundreds more. Its editor has
no login until you set one in its settings file.

entries.name: ntfy
entries.summary: Send notifications to your phone or computer from scripts and apps.
entries.description:
ntfy delivers push notifications. Anything that can make a web request, a
script, a backup job or Uptime Kuma, can send a message to a topic, and the ntfy
app on your phone or desktop shows it. It has no accounts until you configure
them: anyone who can reach it can send and read its topics.

entries.name: Paperless-ngx
entries.summary: Scan, index and archive your paper documents, and find them again.
entries.description: Paperless-ngx is a community-supported open-source document management system that transforms your physical documents into a searchable online archive so you can keep, well, less paper.

entries.name: PhotoPrism
entries.summary: Browse, search and organise your photos, found by place, face and subject.
entries.description:
PhotoPrism indexes the photos and videos in a folder you pick and lets you
browse them by date, place, person and what is in them, without changing the
files. Sign in as admin with the password made up at install. It needs a few
gigabytes of memory while it indexes.

entries.name: Pi-hole
entries.summary: Network-wide Ad Blocking
entries.description:
Pi-hole is a network-wide ad-blocking platform for Linux hardware, using DNS sinkhole technology to protect devices from unwanted content without requiring client-side software. Designed for home or enterprise networks, it offers efficient ad blocking and network optimization.

Core features include network-wide ad blocking and content blocking in non-browser environments. It uses DNS sinkhole to block ads, covering mobile apps and smart TVs. Caching DNS queries speeds up everyday browsing. A command-line interface ensures interoperability with reliable control options.

It provides an intuitive web interface dashboard for viewing and managing system status. An optional DHCP server function automatically protects all devices. Capable of handling high query volumes on server-grade hardware, it supports ad blocking over IPv4 and IPv6. With efficiency and versatility at the core, the platform delivers a modern network protection solution.

**Key Features:**
- Network-wide ad blocking via DNS sinkhole technology
- Blocking content in non-browser environments, including mobile apps and smart TVs
- Caching DNS queries to speed up browsing
- Command-line interface for interoperability
- Intuitive web interface dashboard for system viewing and control
- Optional DHCP server function for automatic device protection
- Ad blocking support for IPv4 and IPv6

**Learn More:**
- [Pi-hole Official Website](https://pi-hole.net/)
- [Pi-hole GitHub](https://github.com/pi-hole/pi-hole)

entries.name: Plex
entries.summary: Stream your films, series and music to every screen, with the Plex apps.
entries.description:
Plex Media Server organises your films, series, music and photos and streams
them to the Plex apps on TVs, phones and browsers. Sign in with your Plex
account on the first visit to claim the server. Hardware transcoding with the
Node's graphics card needs Plex Pass.

settings.label: Run Plex as this group id.
Run Plex as this user id.
Claim token from plex.tv/claim (only without discovery; valid four minutes)

grants.why: Lets the Plex apps on your TVs and phones find the server on your home network, and lets you claim it from the first visit. Its page is then also open on your home network at the Node's address, port 32400.
grants.without: Apps find the server through your Plex account only; claim it with a token from plex.tv/claim (the Claim token setting).

grants.why: Uses the graphics card you picked to convert video for devices that cannot play it as it is, instead of the processor.
grants.without: Video is converted by the processor, more slowly.

entries.name: Prowlarr
entries.summary: Manage the indexers Sonarr and Radarr search, in one place.
entries.description:
Prowlarr keeps your torrent trackers and Usenet indexers in one place and hands them to Sonarr, Radarr and the rest, so you set each up once.
The first visit sets up its login.

entries.name: qBittorrent
entries.summary: Download torrents from a web page, on your own server.
entries.description:
qBittorrent downloads torrents into the shared Downloads folder, where Sonarr
and Radarr pick them up. Sign in as admin; the first password is printed in
the Service's logs when it starts for the first time.

entries.name: Radarr
entries.summary: Keep a list of films you want and fetch them when they are out.
entries.description:
Radarr keeps a list of the films you want, sends them to your download client when they are available and files them in your films folder, named and sorted.
The first visit sets up its login.

entries.name: Sonarr
entries.summary: Follow your series and fetch new episodes as they air.
entries.description:
Sonarr watches for new episodes of the series you follow, sends them to your download client and files them in your series folder, named and sorted.
The first visit sets up its login.

entries.name: Speedtest Tracker
entries.summary: Test your internet speed on a schedule and see how it changes.
entries.description:
Speedtest Tracker runs Ookla's speed test on a schedule and keeps the results,
so you can see your download, upload and ping over days and months. Sign in
first as admin@example.com with the password password, then change both.

settings.label: Key that encrypts its stored secrets
Run Speedtest Tracker as this group id.
Run Speedtest Tracker as this user id.

entries.name: Stirling-PDF
entries.summary: Merge, split, convert, compress and sign PDFs on your own server.
entries.description:
Stirling-PDF is a toolbox for PDF files in the browser: merge and split them,
convert to and from other formats, compress, rotate, add or remove pages, read
text from scans and sign. Files are worked on here and not sent anywhere. Sign
in as admin with the password made up at install.

entries.name: Syncthing
entries.summary: Open decentralized file synchronization
entries.description:
# Unlocking the True Potential of Data Backup

Say goodbye to traditional cloud backup limitations and embrace the future with Syncthing. Unlike conventional cloud services that often come with privacy concerns and storage restrictions, Syncthing provides a secure, real-time file synchronization solution that keeps your data exclusively in your hands. Whether you're syncing work documents or personal photos, you have complete control over where and how your files are stored and shared.

# Features That Make a Difference

Syncthing offers a seamless, user-friendly experience with powerful features designed for everyday users. Enjoy continuous file synchronization between multiple devices without any subscription fees. Experience peace of mind knowing that your data is encrypted and protected from unauthorized access. Syncthing’s open-source nature means no hidden costs, providing a truly transparent and cost-effective solution for your file management needs.

# The Power of Syncthing on Zima

Deploying Syncthing on Zima private cloud devices unlocks unparalleled convenience: enjoy unlimited storage capacity, ensure the privacy of your data, and benefit from blazing local network speeds. Transform your data management and synchronization with the perfect combination of Syncthing’s capabilities and Zima’s powerful infrastructure.

entries.name: Uptime Kuma
entries.summary: Know when your websites and services go down.
entries.description:
A self-hosted monitoring tool with a friendly dashboard. Add the things you
care about and get notified when they stop responding.

entries.name: Vaultwarden
entries.summary: A self-hosted Bitwarden server
entries.description: Alternative implementation of the Bitwarden server API written in Rust and compatible with upstream Bitwarden clients*, perfect for self-hosted deployment where running the official resource-heavy service might not be ideal.

entries.name: Wallabag
entries.summary: Save articles from the web to read later, on any device, without the clutter.
entries.description:
Wallabag saves the articles you want to read later, strips them to their
text and images, and keeps them for its apps and browser extensions. Sign in
first as wallabag with the password wallabag, then change it.
